title: Lift Out, Kick In: Decoupling Event Effects for Time Series Forecasting
abstract: arXiv:2611.27191v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Real-world time series are often shaped by exogenous events whose effects are superimposed on the system's underlying temporal dynamics. Historical observations therefore entangle persistent dynamics with event-induced deviations, making it difficult to determine which patterns should be extrapolated and which should be attributed to specific event contexts. Existing event-aware forecasting methods can incorporate event information or model event-related variation, but typically treat historical event attribution and future event generation separately. We propose Loki (Lift Out, Kick In), a general event-aware forecasting framework built on a shared Event Response Function (ERF). The ERF models event effects according to event type and relative temporal position and is shared across the historical and forecast windows. translated_title: 剔除与注入：面向时间序列预测的事件效应解耦
translated_abstract: 现实世界中的时间序列往往受到外生事件的影响，这些事件的效应叠加在系统固有的时间动态之上。因此，历史观测将持续存在的动态与事件诱发的偏差纠缠在一起，使得难以判断哪些模式应当被外推、哪些应归因于特定的事件情境。现有的事件感知预测方法虽然能够融合事件信息或建模与事件相关的变化，但通常将历史事件归因与未来事件生成分别处理。我们提出 Loki（Lift Out, Kick In），一个基于共享事件响应函数构建的通用事件感知预测框架。该 ERF 根据事件类型和相对时间位置来建模事件效应，并在历史窗口与预测窗口之间共享。Loki 在预测前从历史观测中“剔除”估计得到的事件诱发偏差，然后使用相同的 ERF 将未来事件效应“注入”预测之中。
tldr: 该论文提出基于共享事件响应函数（ERF）的 Loki 框架，通过从历史观测中剔除事件诱发偏差、再向预测中注入未来事件效应，实现事件效应与系统内在时间动态的解耦，从而提升事件感知的时间序列预测性能。
en_tdlr: Loki decouples event effects from underlying temporal dynamics in time series forecasting by sharing a single Event Response Function across historical and forecast windows, lifting out event-induced deviations from past observations and kicking in future event effects.
